messages:
Sanjay: Heads-up — after the routing-policies rollout last night telemetry CPU spiked on collector pods. p99 exporter latency climbed, traces piling up. Anyone else seeing this?

Elaine: yup, saw it on the dashboard. collector-0 CPU went from ~40% -> ~87% around 01:12 UTC. p99 export latency jumped 180ms -> 560ms. spans/sec increased a lot.

Maria: I pulled the spans/sec. Before rollout: ~52k/s. After: ~260k/s. Most growth is small internal spans from the routing layer (route-eval spans), high cardinality attrs (route_id, user_id).

Sam: can we confirm it's not an exporter endpoint slowness? Which exporter? OTLP/gRPC to observability cluster or direct to our trace-store?

Elaine: OTLP/gRPC to obs-cluster via internal LB. Exporter queue depth went from <10 -> 14k queued. Exporter CPU time also high. Looks like batching params are too small and concurrency limited.

Irene: quick idea: drop some low-value spans (status OK internal routing) or apply route-level sampling. We need to avoid losing the critical spans though.

Sanjay: agree. Short-term mitigation: increase batch processor size & schedule_delay, and turn on tail_sampling to keep 1 in N traces for high-volume routes.

Maria: tried increasing batch_size from 512 -> 2048 and schedule_delay_millis 200 -> 1000 on a canary collector. Export throughput improved, queue drained, CPU dropped ~30% on that pod.

Sam: nice. Any measurable effect on p99 export latency on canary?

Maria: p99 fell from 560ms -> 220ms on the canary. But note increased memory usage for batch buffer.

Irene: memory-limiter in collector config prevented OOM, but we should be careful. Also recommend attribute-denormalization filter: drop route_id and user_id from span attributes for these route-eval spans (or hash them to low-cardinality keys).

Sanjay: we should also consider adaptive dropping: have a span-dropper that keeps top-K routes by traffic and samples the rest aggressively. That preserves signal for popular routes.

Sam: can we prototype an otel-collector processor that drops spans by metricized thresholds? Example heuristic: if route spans/sec > 10k, keep 10% of spans except those with errors.

Elaine: wrote a quick config prototype to test locally:

```
processors:
  batch:
    timeout: 1000ms
    send_batch_size: 2048
  memory_limiter:
    limit_mib: 2048
    spike_limit_mib: 512
  filter/span_dropper:
    match_type: strict
    rules:
      - name: drop-route-eval
        span_names: ["route_evaluate", "route_score"]
        attributes:
          - key: "http.route"
            op: exists
        drop_fraction: 0.9
```

Maria: test run shows ~60% reduction in spans emitted to exporter for route-eval spans with negligible impact on error traces.

Irene: we should also add a route-label aggregator to reduce cardinality: replace full route path with route group (e.g., /checkout/:id -> /checkout/:param). That will help downstream indexing costs.

Sanjay: agree. Action plan:
- short-term (hotfix): apply batch increase + schedule_delay on all collectors, enable memory limiter (SRE). (assigned: Elaine)
- mid-term: implement span-dropper + route grouping in collector (eng-platform + eng-runtime). (assigned: Sam, Maria)
- long-term: adaptive sampler + observability for sampling decisions + rollout UX to let product teams opt-in per-route. (assigned: Sanjay, Irene)

ops-bot: Incident INC-4122 created: "Telemetry collector CPU & p99 regression after routing rollout". Pager on-call.

Elaine: applying hotfix to staging now, will roll to prod if staging looks good. kubectl patch configmap otel-collector-config -n telemetry --patch "{...}" to update. I left a snippet in the incident ticket.

Sam: +1. We should also add alerting: spans-queued > 10k OR exporter_p99 > 400ms -> page.

Maria: logging note: we found one microservice emitting nested spans every decision loop (0.5ms each) that were previously sampled out. We need a code change to reduce span creation upstream too. Filed GH PR #1287.

Irene: good catch. That'll reduce raw volume at source.

Sanjay: cool. If staging hotfix looks good, we'll coordinate a controlled rollback of the routing-policies rollout to avoid more noise. Will also prep a postmortem with metrics: spans/sec delta, collector CPU, exporter p99, memory.

Elaine: staging hotfix shows spans/sec reduced to ~120k and collector CPU ~52%. Rolling to prod in 10m.

Maria: keeping an eye on trace-store ingestion costs — if we keep raw volume up we'll blow budget even if exporter latency is fixed.

Sanjay: thanks all. Please add any config diffs to the ticket and ping me once prod is stable. :thumbsup:
